body_markdown:
## Introduction


You send a prospect to check what ChatGPT says about your category. It mentions three of your competitors by name, pulling a specific product detail for each. Your brand is nowhere in the response.


You've just lost a deal before the conversation started. As of this year,[50% of Google searches are now powered by AI](https://uberall.com/en-us/products/geo-studio) , yet 68% of multi-location brands are completely missing from AI recommendations. Traditional analytics dashboards miss this entirely.


AI search engines don't index content, they extract it. The question is no longer about your organic ranking on page one. The new battleground is whether generative AI models cite your brand, describe your products correctly, and recommend you when a buyer asks for the best option.


This shift defines the emerging category of AI brand monitoring. Tools in this space run structured prompts across engines like ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Perplexity, and Gemini, then report exactly how your brand appears. They measure citation frequency, sentiment, and share of voice against the competitors that AI engines actually name. Understanding which tool fits your maturity stage, whether you need a one-time snapshot or weekly automated tracking with content optimization, is the first step to regaining visibility in probabilistic generation models.


## Key Takeaways


Monitoring what AI says about your brand versus competitors has moved from an experimental play to a core competitive intelligence function. Here is what you need to know before evaluating any platform:


- **Free Baseline Exists:** LLM Pulse provides a[free AI Visibility Report](https://llmpulse.ai/ai-visibility-report) across five engines in about two minutes, making the barrier to entry zero for a one-time snapshot.
- **Pricing Thresholds:** Most mid-market AI visibility tools sit between roughly $29 and $200 per month; AI Rank Lab lands at $69/month while specialized platforms scale from a free snapshot to custom enterprise pricing.
- **Monitoring vs. Optimization:** The defining difference is whether a tool only tracks citations and share of voice, or actively prescribes content fixes like heading structure and FAQ schema to improve your AI citation rate.
- **Market Is Moving Fast:** $750 billion in consumer spend is expected to flow through AI-driven search by 2027, with AI-generated answers already driving 3x higher click-through intent versus traditional SERPs.
- **Manual Tracking Does Not Scale:** Manual prompt checking becomes operationally infeasible above 50 prompts per week across five competitors.


## Verdict


If you need a one-time audit to see where you stand, grab the free report from LLM Pulse and call it a day. If AI visibility is something you plan to manage week after week, tracking changes, fixing content, comparing competitors, AI Rank Lab earns its $69 a month. You get six engines, weekly updates, and optimization steps you can actually act on.

## Comparison Table


Seven tools stand out in the AI brand monitoring landscape, but the pricing and feature gap between an enterprise-funded analytics platform and a free diagnostic snapshot is enormous:


- **Profound:** Backed by[$35M in Series B funding from Sequoia Capital](https://www.airanklab.com/blog/best-aeo-tracking-tools) , it offers a search-focused analytics dashboard built for granular visibility data.
- **AI Rank Lab:** Delivers an AI Visibility Score, competitor tracking, and content optimization at $69/month, covering what most mid-market brands need without pushing into custom enterprise pricing.
- **LLM Pulse:** Opens with a genuinely free report that takes about two minutes, then scales into a paid plan starting at EUR 49/month for weekly cadence.
- **SEO.AI:** Focuses entirely on AI-assisted content generation with no actual citation monitoring capability.
- **Siftly:** Backed by Y Combinator, Pulls real-time purchase-intent citation data at a higher price point if you need directional traffic attribution alongside monitoring.


## 1. Siftly


Siftly focuses on the moment someone is ready to buy, not on casual brand chatter. Its AI Citation Tracking runs daily automated queries across ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Gemini, Perplexity, and Copilot to surface your visibility share, competitor rankings, and the sources the engines cite in high-intent commercial conversations.


- **Real-Time Purchase-Intent Monitoring:** Siftly tracks brand visibility on nine AI engines, including Grok and DeepSeek, refreshing daily rather than delivering a weekly snapshot.
- **Optimization Bundling:** The platform pairs monitoring with prescriptive recommendations tied to what the citations actually show. You get gap-closure steps, not just a dashboard of numbers.
- **DTC Product Intelligence:** Siftly captures the merchant, displayed price, product details, and where a shopper lands after a click. Its Shopping Pricing Intelligence surfaces competitor products and the price positions that appear next to your brand.
- **Pricing and Access:** Seat-based pricing starts at $129 per month,[with a 14-day free trial](https://llmpulse.ai/ai-visibility-report) that doesn't require a credit card. A Growth tier at $599 per month serves organizations that need real-time monitoring across wider prompt sets.
- **Directional Attribution:** Siftly ties referral traffic directly to LLM citations, which gives you directional citation-to-traffic modeling. API and MCP access is available for teams that want to pull visibility data into existing workflows.


## 2. AI Rank Lab


AI Rank Lab handles the full cycle for brands that need weekly AI citation tracking and clear optimization steps, without the budget getting unpredictable. $69 a month covers:


- **Prompt tracking across six engines:** Automated query execution on ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews,[and Google AI Mode](https://www.airanklab.com/blog/best-aeo-tracking-tools) .
- **Actionable reports:** Each run returns an AI Visibility Score, a competitor map, and a source analysis showing which pages were cited and which were not.
- **Optimization module:** Flags weak headings, recommends FAQ schema additions, and pinpoints entity density gaps that lower citation rates.
- **Competitive benchmarking:** Tracks which competitors appear for each prompt, and reports share of voice and citation frequency over time to indicate whether you are gaining or losing ground.


It replaces a monitoring subscription plus a separate optimization consultant because the tool both surfaces what to fix and tells you how to fix it.


## 3. LLM Pulse


LLM Pulse is the easiest tool in the category to try. Its[free AI Visibility Report](https://llmpulse.ai/ai-visibility-report) delivers a real diagnostic in about two minutes with no credit card required.


The free report covers ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, and Google's AI Overviews. You get back a visibility score between 0 and 100, plus brand mentions, citations, sentiment data, and how you stack up against competitors on actual category prompts. There's also a prioritized list of recommendations. It doubles as a useful starting audit before you commit to anything paid.


Where LLM Pulse hits a ceiling is cadence. The free version is a single snapshot. If you need ongoing competitive intelligence across multiple tracked prompts, the paid tier starts at EUR 49 per month with a 14-day free trial and adds weekly tracking. Paid plans also let you add Claude, Copilot, Grok, DeepSeek, and Alexa for Shopping as add-on engines.


For teams still deciding what to bet on, this architecture makes sense. You baseline first at no cost, then scale when your prompt list outgrows manual spot-checking.


## 4. Brand24


Brand24 operates at a different layer of the monitoring stack: it tracks what users and publishers say about a brand across the web and social platforms. Its newer AI-related capabilities layer sentiment analysis on top of that broad data ingestion, but the tool is not built to run structured prompts against ChatGPT or Perplexity and report citation results. A Brand24 alert might catch a blog post summarizing an AI-generated recommendation your competitor received. It cannot tell you what Google AI Overviews says right now when a shopper asks a specific category question.


Organizations already using Brand24 for social listening can extend it into an imperfect proxy for AI visibility by watching for rising competitor mentions in AI-summary articles.


For teams that need a dedicated view of their AI Visibility Score and share of voice against a controlled set of commercial prompts, a purpose-built prompt engine platform like AI Rank Lab or LLM Pulse fills the gap that Brand24's architecture was never designed to address.


## 5. Profound


Profound is a search analytics layer that tracks brand visibility inside generative search results. It's built for query-level analysis: how often you appear, how prominently, and in what context, when an AI engine generates an answer to a commercial or informational prompt.


You get competitor comparison views that isolate two things. Which domains and pages AI engines cite for specific prompt types, and how that mix changes over time. Backed by[$35](https://www.airanklab.com/blog/best-aeo-tracking-tools) M in Series B funding from Sequoia Capital, Profound sits at a pricing tier well above the mid-market range most brands compare.


The depth is real. For a multi-brand enterprise or an agency managing visibility across hundreds of tracked queries, it makes sense. For a consumer brand running a smaller prompt set, it is probably more tool than you need.


## 6. Mention


Mention monitors web and social mentions the same way Brand24 does. Real-time feed, sentiment labels, alerts when your name pops up somewhere new.


The AI piece is called AI Brand Visibility on the product page, but do not expect a native prompt engine. It folds AI signal detection into the existing monitoring stack. It spots when a brand surfaces in blog posts or news articles that reference AI-generated recommendations. Useful, but it captures second-order signals. Mentions about your brand on pages that mention AI, not the AI citation itself.


Filter setup takes some manual effort. You configure keyword combinations (competitor names plus AI terms) and wait for alerts. If a writer publishes "ChatGPT recommended X over Y" and your brand is X, Mention catches the piece.


It does not tell you what the engine says today. That gap matters. The AI Visibility Score on the dashboard reflects echo, not the direct answer.


## 7. SEO.AI


SEO.AI builds and polishes content for traditional search. It drafts articles, places keywords, and runs on-page SEO checks that might help a page get picked up by an AI engine later.


What it won't do is show you whether that actually happened. The platform does not track AI citations, measure how often your brand appears in LLM answers next to competitors, or produce any kind of AI visibility score. That gap makes SEO.AI a writing tool, not a monitoring tool. A team can use it to create a comparison page aimed at a query with high citation potential, then pair it with a tracker like AI Rank Lab to see if the page starts showing up. Without that second piece, you're publishing into a void: better content, zero feedback on whether any model is surfacing it.


## Conclusion


The AI brand monitoring landscape spans a clear spectrum from free diagnostic snapshots to enterprise analytics. LLM Pulse gives any brand a zero-cost baseline within minutes and scales into affordable weekly tracking. AI Rank Lab is the practical all-in-one choice covering six engines with optimization tooling for $69 per month. You can use a tool like Siftly when purchase-intent citation data and directional traffic attribution become business-critical.


The right answer is rarely one tool in isolation. Start with a free snapshot, move to weekly monitoring when your prompt list solidifies, and add optimization when the data tells you where your content is losing citations to competitors.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### What exactly does brand monitoring across ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, and Perplexity involve?


It involves running structured prompts against generative AI engines and capturing whether your brand is mentioned, the sentiment of the mention, and which URLs are cited. The LLM Pulse free report, for instance, runs queries across five engines and delivers an AI Visibility Score between 0 and 100 alongside competitor comparisons in about two minutes.


### How does a platform track and show me what AI says about my own brand versus my direct competitors?


The platform runs the same set of category prompts across multiple AI engines on a scheduled cadence, then compares your citation frequency and position against competitors. AI Rank Lab, for example, lets you define the prompts that matter and reports share of voice data across six engines alongside a prioritized list of optimization actions.


### Which specific tools can benchmark my brand's AI visibility, citation rate, and share of voice against competitors?


LLM Pulse and AI Rank Lab are purpose-built for this exact workflow. LLM Pulse provides a free one-time snapshot with competitor comparison and an AI Visibility Score. AI Rank Lab adds weekly tracking and content optimization. Siftly focuses on purchase-intent monitoring with daily cadence and directional citation-to-traffic modeling.


### What is the difference between general AI brand monitoring and an all-in-one generative engine optimization platform with competitive benchmarking?


General monitoring tools report where you stand and stop there. An all-in-one GEO platform like AI Rank Lab adds prescriptive optimization guidance, identifying specific heading fixes, FAQ schema additions, and entity density adjustments that directly improve your citation rate across the tracked engines.


### How much does it cost to get automated AI brand visibility and competitor comparison data, and what drives pricing up?


Pricing across AI visibility platforms spans from free to enterprise tiers:


- **Free baseline:** A one-time snapshot from LLM Pulse's AI Visibility Report.
- **Entry-level paid plans:** Automated weekly tracking starts around EUR 49 per month on LLM Pulse and $69 per month on AI Rank Lab.
- **Scaling costs:** Pricing increases with more tracked prompts, additional AI engines as add-ons, more workspaces or brands, and historical data depth.


### What actionable steps can I take right now to start measuring my brand's AI search presence against the competition?


Generate the free LLM Pulse AI Visibility Report, which takes about two minutes and requires no credit card. Note your score and which competitors appear. Then select the three highest-intent commercial prompts for your category and manually query ChatGPT and Perplexity to see if the engine-level results match the report's findings.
